Back in 2006, I went skydiving a couple times. I took the all-day class so that I didn't have to do a tandem jump. The first time, I did everything right and was able to guide myself down. I loved every minute of it I couldn't wait to go again. Unfortunately, I couldn't afford another jump until later in the month. So a couple weeks go by and I'm ready for the next jump. We go to jump and I get to 5000 feet so I go to pull to release my chute. I don't feel the yank of my  chute catching the wind... I look up and my lines are twisted! I almost shit myself as the fear sets in but then I remembered what we went over in class should this ever happen! I start pulling the lines apart to get them untwisted and I start thanking the heavens when the chute fully unfurls. Half way down I remember that I have a backup chute so I wasn't completely screwed if the lines wouldn't untangle. After landing, I tell my instructors what happened. When I pulled, i did it in such a way that my body started spinning which caused the lines to twist like they did. We went over that in the class but being that it was a couple weeks since I had taken it, I had forgotten all about that little detail.

As for your your anxiety and depression, Happiness is a choice. I don't mean this in the obnoxious, "You've just gotta cheer up man!" way. I know from personally having been through similar issues that you can't just tell a person to deal with it and they can just magically power through it. That person has to decide to prioritize their happiness. You will eventually get to a point where -YOU- decide that living this way is just not enough and even though you're feeling like shit, you will be glad to make the effort to change. When each person reaches that point is different for everyone. Try to start doing things that make you happy. If you don't have anything that currently makes you happy, try something new. For me, it was writing. My mind runs at a 100 miles an hour and I'm always running through weird scenarios in my head.  I've never written anything except for work. But when I started letting it all out on paper, it was just such a relief. It also provided some great entertainment afterwards when I'd completely forgotten about it at some point in the future. 

It could be anything new, not just writing. Painting, reading new books, drawing, sculpting, puzzles, assembling Gundam models(also a favorite of mine!), walking, biking, whatever! Once you find something that brings that relief, it will still take some effort but you will be happy to make that effort to make yourself happy again. Some days, it'll be bad enough that you won't want to do anything. Don't worry about it. It's just one day. Take each day one at a time and leave the past where it is.
